You touch a door handle and zap! Why does that mostly happen in winter?
Every time you walk across a carpet or pull off a sweater, tiny electrons jump from one material to another.
Without noticing, you slowly fill up with electric charge.

text: Wait. Thousands of volts? Then why doesn't it zap you in summer?

You see, in summer the air is humid. An invisible thin layer of water sits on everything and quietly drains your charge away.
But cold winter air holds much less water. And heating it up inside doesn't add any.
So the charge has nowhere to go. Until you touch metal.

text: Zap. All of it at once.
Want fewer zaps? Keep your room between thirty and fifty percent humidity.
